traceability.evidence:
Implementation: - Rule file src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts exists and is explicitly tagged with this story: - JSDoc: `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`, `@req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION`, `@req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`. - Exports an ESLint RuleModule with: - meta.type: "problem". - meta.docs.description: "Require @story and @req annotations on code branches". - meta.fixable: "code" (auto-fix support). - meta.messages: { missingAnnotation: "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}." } (clear, targeted message). - meta.schema: object with optional `branchTypes` array, `uniqueItems: true`, `additionalProperties: false` (option validation). - create(context): - Calls `validateBranchTypes(context)` from ../utils/branch-annotation-helpers. - If validateBranchTypes returns a listener (invalid config case), returns it directly (config error path). - Otherwise iterates each allowed branch type and installs a handler that: - Skips `SwitchCase` where `node.test == null` (default case) so default cases are not forced to be annotated. - Calls `reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef)` for each branch node.
Branch analysis and helpers: - File src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts implements the technical requirements: - DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES (tagged with this story and REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA): - `["IfStatement", "SwitchCase", "TryStatement", "CatchClause", "ForStatement", "ForOfStatement", "ForInStatement", "WhileStatement", "DoWhileStatement"]`. - Covers if/else, switch cases, try/catch, and loop branches as specified by REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION. - validateBranchTypes(context) (tagged with REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE): - Reads `context.options[0].branchTypes`. - Filters out invalid entries using DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES. - If any invalid types exist: - Returns a RuleListener `{ Program(node) { ... } }` that reports for each invalid type: - `message: "Value \"${t}\" should be equal to one of the allowed values: ${DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES.join(", ")}"`. - This aligns with the story’s requirement to fail fast on invalid configuration. - Otherwise returns either the user-provided branchTypes (narrowed) or DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES. - gatherBranchCommentText(sourceCode, node) (tagged with REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION): - For SwitchCase: - Uses `sourceCode.lines` and a PRE_COMMENT_OFFSET of 2 lines. - Walks upward with a while loop collecting lines starting with `//` or `/*` until a non-comment is reached. - Returns concatenated comment text, allowing comments separated by blank lines close to the case. - For other branch nodes: - Uses `sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node)` and maps `comment.value` to a combined string. - getBranchAnnotationInfo(...): - Uses gatherBranchCommentText to compute `text` and determine: - `missingStory = !/@story\b/.test(text)`; - `missingReq = !/@req\b/.test(text)`. - Derives indentation from the line where the branch starts and computes `insertPos` via `getIndexFromLoc`. - reportMissingStory(...) and reportMissingReq(...) (tagged with REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING): - If first missing @story in the current context (`storyFixCountRef.count === 0`): - Reports `messageId: "missingAnnotation"` with `data: { missing: "@story" }`. - Supplies a fixer that inserts `// @story .story.md` with proper indentation before the branch. - Increments `storyFixCountRef.count` to avoid multiple implicit story insertions. - For @req when @story is already present: - Inserts `// @req ` before the branch. - Otherwise reports missing @req without a fixer (to avoid stacking auto-fixes when story is absent). - reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef): - Obtains `missingStory`, `missingReq`, `indent`, `insertPos`. - Iterates over an actions array (story and req) and calls the respective reporter if the annotation is missing. - Design is agnostic to nesting, so nested branches are handled naturally.
Tests (behavior and coverage for this story): - File tests/rules/require-branch-annotation.test.ts: - Header JSDoc explicitly ties tests to this story and requirements: - `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`. - `@req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION` and error-related requirements from story 007.0. - Uses `RuleTester` from ESLint with `languageOptions: { parserOptions: { ecmaVersion: 2020 } }`. - `describe("Require Branch Annotation Rule (Story 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS)", ...)` for traceability. - Valid cases verify correct behavior for each significant branch type: - IfStatement, ForStatement, WhileStatement, DoWhileStatement, ForOfStatement, ForInStatement. - SwitchCase scenarios with annotations immediately above and with a blank line before the case (tests comment association logic). - Try-finally and try-catch annotated separately. - Default SwitchCase without annotations explicitly valid (proves the `node.test == null` guard is effective). - Custom branchTypes options demonstrating that unlisted branch types are ignored, and listed ones enforced (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE). - Invalid cases test detection and auto-fix: - Missing both @story and @req on multiple branch types, asserting two separate errors and expected transformed outputs including `// @story .story.md` and, where applicable, `// @req `. - Missing only @req when @story is present, verifying that only @req is added and only one error is reported. - Missing only @story when @req is present, verifying @story insertion and correct error message. - Try-catch where both try and catch are missing annotations, verifying multiple errors and behavior over a more complex control structure (nested handling). - Invalid configuration (`branchTypes: ["UnknownType"]`) verifying that misconfiguration produces a schema/validation error with message matching `/should be equal to one of the allowed values/`.
Integration into plugin and presets: - File src/index.ts: - RULE_NAMES includes "require-branch-annotation", so the rule is available to ESLint via the plugin. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES maps `"traceability/require-branch-annotation"` to "error". - configs.recommended and configs.strict both use createTraceabilityFlatConfig(), which includes `"traceability/require-branch-annotation": "error"` in rules, ensuring the rule is active in both presets by default. - File docs/config-presets.md documents that `traceability/require-branch-annotation` is enabled at severity `error` in both recommended and strict presets.
User/documentation coverage: - File docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md: - References this story and its key requirements: - `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`. - `@req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION`, `@req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`. - Describes rule purpose: ensures significant code branches (if/else, switch cases, loops, try/catch) have `@story` and `@req` annotations. - Describes options (branchTypes), default and allowed values, and invalid configuration behavior (error message for invalid types) consistent with implementation. - Provides clear Correct, Incorrect, and Invalid Configuration examples that match rule semantics.

traceability.notes: Story 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS is fully implemented and integrated. The require-branch-annotation rule exists, is wired into the plugin and presets, and uses helper utilities to detect and analyze all specified branch types. It associates comments with branches, parses @story and @req, supports configuration of branch types with validation and clear configuration error messages, and provides auto-fix behavior for the first missing @story and for missing @req when @story exists. Tests comprehensively cover valid and invalid scenarios across if/else, switch cases, try/catch, and loop branches, including configuration error paths. Documentation for the rule and for configuration presets aligns with the code and references this story and its requirements. All acceptance criteria in the story (core functionality, quality, integration, user experience, error handling, and documentation) are satisfied, so the assessment status is PASSED.
